after: lrc-retest.md R4b: production's fade-to-value replayed through its own engine and strategy code (the untuned baseline, committed and reported before this was run)
question: does fade-to-value fit the structures service if the two are tuned to each other? Fade-to-value consumes exactly what structures publishes: levels with touches, probability, strength, zones, vol_bps and risk_vol
data: the replay logs of lrc_fade.py: for each series and source (real, iid walk, GARCH walk) the 15m bars, every actionable call, and every 15m / 30m call with the valuation book (the levels production's FadeToValue held: price, interval, probability, strength, touches, last seen) within 12 vol units of spot
decision: for each logged 15m / 30m call: value = the book level with the most touches (ties to the nearest) among those passing the value definition; distance d = (value - spot) / unit, unit = spot x vol_bps / 10000; trade toward value when |d| >= min distance; stop = production's stop_for(the call's level, side, multiple x risk_vol x unit, zone edge, clearance x unit); refused when price is already past the stop or the target is behind price (as production)

search_notes.min_strength_q: a quantile of the strength of every book level in the real discovery logs (0 = no threshold)
search_notes.max_age_h: hours since the book last saw the level (production forgets at 6)
search_notes.level_intervals: which timeframes a value level may come from: all, 1h/2h/4h only (the context timeframes), 2h/4h only
search_notes.min_agree: distinct timeframes the book holds within 0.35 vol (production's merge distance) of the value level, itself included
search_notes.target: the value minus a buffer of 0.25 (production), 0 (the full value) or 0.5 vol units; or no target and a 2-unit trail behind completed bars' best high
search_notes.trend: LRC(100) slope sign on 1h bars resampled from the 15m bars, at the last completed 1h bar: none, trade with it, trade against it
search_notes.regime: structures' own vol_stretch feature on the call: none, below 1 (low), 1 or above (high)
search_notes.entry_interval: the call's timeframe; context is the level-interval dimension above
search_notes.hold: production's 4h (16 15m bars), out at the close if neither stop nor target
search_notes.not searched: production's quality() gates (stateful percentile floors; left at off, as R4b CORE), break-even and trail protection, sizing

production_default_in_the_space: touches>=4, prob>=0, strength q0, age<=6h, levels all, agree>=1, max 8, min 1.5, clearance 0.25, x1 risk_vol, target value-0.25, entry both, trend none, regime none

objective.data: discovery only: the 12 Binance perpetuals before 2024-01-01 (the only 15m history before 2024)
objective.score: mean R after costs over the discovery trades
objective.eligible: P(+2R before the stop, within the hold) at or above the same configuration's on the reference walk: the iid walk for real data; for the walks, the other walk
objective.trades: every qualifying call is a trade (overlaps allowed) during tuning; confirmation reports this and one-open-trade-per-series

walks: the identical search and objective run on the iid and the GARCH walk logs; the best walk configuration's in-sample score is the overfitting allowance

confirm.data: 2024-01-01 onward: the 12 Binance perpetuals (same symbols, unseen time) and every class the tuning never saw (FX, METAL, INDEX, ENERGY, CRYPTO_CFD, DERIV_1S, DERIV_DIFFUSIVE, DERIV_JUMPY, RANGE_BREAK, reported apart; the non-Deriv unseen pool judged)
confirm.passes_if: the single selected configuration: R > 0 after costs with its 90% day-bootstrap interval above 0 on confirmation (Binance 2024+ and the unseen non-Deriv pool, each), R > 0 in discovery, its discovery score above the walks' best in-sample score (the allowance), its confirmation R above the walks' own tuned configurations on their confirmation data and above the untuned R4b baseline (production's defaults, CORE) on the same data
confirm.multiplicity: BH at q = 0.10 over the top-5 configurations x the two confirmation sets; the search size (497,664) is stated beside every number

holds.question: do structures' quality scores predict a level's hold rate beyond walks?
holds.calls: every actionable call in the logs, every timeframe
holds.hold: the side price arrived from: from above (support) HOLD when a high reaches level + 1 unit before a close at or below level - 1 unit, from below mirrored; scanned on 15m bars from the first bar after the call, up to 500 bars; undecided dropped
holds.called: the call's own direction (up / down) reaching 1 unit before a close 1 unit the other way
holds.deciles: of probability and of strength, cut on the real discovery calls (Binance before 2024) and applied unchanged to everything, walks included
holds.reading: a top decile that holds clearly more than the same decile on walks is the mechanism the strategy needs; if not, no tuning can create one
